subject: VPC support mileposts, implementation credit & failover ops
messages:
From: Procurement Team <procurement@acmehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-16T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Pricing and support model for VPC deployment — clarification

Hi Ben,

Thanks for the demo last week. Before we move to procurement, two quick clarifications so our T&Cs and finance team can model this:

1) Platform fee treatment — Acme capitalizes platform fees over 36 months. Do you have an itemized SKU that lets us separate the implementation/onboarding component (one-time) from the ongoing platform fee (recurring)?
2) Implementation credit — you mentioned a potential implementation credit tied to a committed node pool. Is that an up-front credit, or a staged credit tied to milestones?
3) Support model — we need to understand the delta between a ticketed time-and-materials model vs a retainer/on-call model (pricing, response SLA, how credits apply).

Could you send a short breakdown (line items + suggested amortization labels) we can attach to the PO?

Appreciate it — Alex
Procurement, Acme Health

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Procurement Team <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@acmehealth.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-16T12:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pricing and support model for VPC deployment — clarification

Alex — thanks, great questions. High-level answers inline, attaching a simple workbook and draft SOW for finance.

1) Platform fee: we split pricing into three invoiceable components (suggested accounting treatment in parentheses):
   - Implementation/onboarding (one-time, capitalize) — SOW professional services line item.
   - Platform entitlement (recurring, amortize) — monthly platform fee per cluster/node.
   - Support retainer (optional, recurring, could be OPEX) — on-call retainer or block-hours.

2) Implementation credit: we can apply a staged credit tied to milestones. Typical structure: 50% credit applied on Go-Live acceptance, 25% at month 3 production milestone, 25% at month 6. We can also convert to an up-front credit against the first invoice if you prefer that for PO simplicity.

3) Support model: two options —
   A) Ticketed (T&M): pay-as-you-go for engineering hours (lower baseline cost, variable). Response SLAs per ticket severity; standard business hours for lower severities.
   B) Retainer/on-call: fixed monthly fee for guaranteed on-call coverage (24/7 options) and faster response SLAs. Includes a small number of included engineering hours; overage billed at reduced T&M rate.

I'm looping Soojin for SRE/on-call SLAs and Marissa for the commercial numbers.

Next steps: we can produce a 1-page commercial summary with line item SKUs and an amortization suggestion for your accounting team. Looking at your usage profile from the pilot, I can also propose two price buckets (starter vs committed node pool) so finance can compare.

Best,
Ben
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: SOW-acme-v3.pdf; implementation-workbook.xlsx
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@acmehealth.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-16T14:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pricing and support model for VPC deployment — clarification

Alex / team — adding operational detail on SLAs and failover behavior so you can map to your risk registers.

Ticketed (T&M):
- Response SLA: Sev 1 — 2 hours business hours (NBD partial cover); Sev 2 — 4 hours BH; Sev 3 — next business day.
- Failover: we provide runbooks and a 2-hour patching window for critical hotfixes; failover to a standby region is handled as an engagement (T&M) unless you purchase replication + automatic failover add-on.

Retainer / On-call:
- Response SLA: Sev 1 — 30 minutes (24/7); Sev 2 — 2 hours 24/7; Sev 3 — 4 hours BH.
- Failover: included for customers that opt for our "Failover Assurance" add-on (active-active or warm-standby) — this is priced separately and is typically capitalized as infrastructure but the service element is recurring.

Implementation credits: We prefer staged credits tied to acceptance milestones (makes it auditable). If Acme needs a single-line PO credit for finance, we can issue an up-front credit but will record the same milestone constraints internally.

I'll propose two concrete bundles in the commercial summary:
- Bundle A: Starter (no retainer) — lower platform fee, T&M support.
- Bundle B: Committed (reserve node pool) + retainer + Failover Assurance add-on — higher upfront commit, deeper implementation credit, SLA uplift.

Sooj
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@acmehealth.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-17T09:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pricing and support model for VPC deployment — clarification

Alex — attaching the commercial summary you asked for (quick bullets here):

Proposed commercial lines (list price / example):
- Implementation/onboarding (one-time): $85,000 (can be labeled capital expenditure)
- Platform entitlement (recurring): $12,500 / month per committed cluster (metered if uncommitted)
- Support retainer (optional): $10,000 / month for 24/7 retainer with up to 40 included hours; overage $250/hr.
- Failover Assurance add-on: $6,000 / month for warm-standby + runbook validations.

Implementation credit options:
- Staged credit (recommended): 50% on Go-Live, 25% @30 days prod, 25% @90 days prod.
- Up-front credit: we can place a $25k up-front credit on invoice one (reduces AP workflow friction).

Discounts: for a 36-month amortized deal with a 12-node committed pool we can offer a 12% discount on platform entitlement and include the $25k up-front credit. If Acme prefers shorter amortization we can shift credit timing but discount is tied to term and commit.

Docs attached: SOW-acme-v3.pdf, commercial-summary-acme.pdf (both stub references in workbook).

If this looks good, Ben and I will prepare a PO-ready line-item export and a DocuSign-ready SOW.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Commercials — Redwood Inference

- We prefer a single PO with an amortization note referencing the implementation line (capex) and the monthly platform fee (opex). If you can supply an exportable CSV of invoice line-items with suggested GL mapping that would be ideal.
- The up-front $25k credit option is helpful. Can you confirm whether that reduces the initial invoice only (i.e., not reducing the staged acceptance credits)?
- For accounting, we also need the DocuSign SOW and a named Redwood billing contact for AP (contact + email).

If you can send the PO-ready CSV and DocuSign link by EOD Friday we can route to Finance for the PO creation.

Alex
